title: BLF: Add padding to last log object when closing log container.
description:
Keeps last object header and its position on disk in the writer data.
When log container then is closed the last object can be expanded,
to allow the start and end of log containers to be 4 byte aligned.

Fixes #21017

AI-Assisted: no

notes.body:
This change will go unnoticeable for Wireshark users, but will improve the compatibility with other tools (primarily verified with Vector's tools) as mentioned in the referenced issue.

From the Wireshark perspective I've made sure we're not losing considerable performance by tracking the object headers:
```
Read 10000001 potential packets, wrote 10000001 packets (750004795 bytes including overhead).
../gendata-released.sh  70.06s user 15.54s system 177% cpu 48.308 total
```
prior to the patch compared to
```
Read 10000001 potential packets, wrote 10000001 packets (750006002 bytes including overhead).
../gendata-patched.sh  69.72s user 15.05s system 178% cpu 47.431 total
```
thus the added tracking seems to have less effect than what else my computer is doing at the same time.

As this change backtracks and updates the block header for a earlier written object, I've also checked what type of objects we currently can write, to ensure all of them do have either fixed data length or a proper length indicator in the object header itself, so the objects won't fail parsing due to the block header compensating for the padding.

```
BLF_OBJTYPE_APP_TEXT - blf_apptext_t.textLength
BLF_OBJTYPE_ETHERNET_FRAME - blf_ethernetframeheader_t.payloadlength
BLF_OBJTYPE_CAN_XL_CHANNEL_FRAME - blf_canxlchannelframe_t.dataLength
BLF_OBJTYPE_CAN_FD_MESSAGE_64 - blf_canfdmessage64_t.validDataBytes
BLF_OBJTYPE_CAN_MESSAGE - fixed struct size, max payload size allocated in struct
BLF_OBJTYPE_FLEXRAY_RCVMESSAGE - blf_flexrayrcvmessage_t.payloadLength
BLF_OBJTYPE_LIN_MESSAGE - fixed struct size, max payload size allocated in struct
```

Additionally, to make sure we're as unaligned as possible, for every type of object to end up at odd offets, the following test steps generates the worst possible combination of blf files with regards to compatibility with other tools:
```
# First generate files for all records type
( for i in $(seq 1 3) ; do printf '0:00:00.%06d\n' $i ; echo '0000   00 00 00 e7 03 05 00 00 00 11 22' ; done ) | text2pcap -E socketcan -F blf - testrun/test-canfd-3x-3b.blf
( for i in $(seq 1 3) ; do printf '0:00:00.%06d\n' $i ; echo '0000   00 00 00 e7 03 00 00 00 00 11 22' ; done ) | text2pcap -E socketcan -F blf - testrun/test-can-3x-3b.blf
( for i in $(seq 1 3) ; do printf '0:00:00.%06d\n' $i ; echo '0000   00 00 00 e7 80 00 03 00 00 00 00 00 00 11 22' ; done ) | text2pcap -E socketcan -F blf - testrun/test-canxl-3x-3b.blf
( for i in $(seq 1 3) ; do printf '0:00:00.%06d\n' $i ; echo '0000   01 00 00 00 30 12 00 00 00 11 22' ; done ) | text2pcap -E lin -F blf - testrun/test-lin-3x-3b.blf
( for i in $(seq 1 3) ; do printf '0:00:00.%06d\n' $i ; echo '0000   01 00 00 00 50 12 00 00 00 11 22 33 44' ; done ) | text2pcap -E lin -F blf - testrun/test-lin-3x-5b.blf
( for i in $(seq 1 3) ; do printf '0:00:00.%06d\n' $i ; echo '0000   01 00 00 e7 06 00 2a 00 11 22 33 44 55' ; done ) | text2pcap -E flexray -F blf - testrun/test-flexray-3x-6b.blf
( for i in $(seq 1 3) ; do printf '0:00:00.%06d\n' $i ; echo '0000   00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09 0a 0b 0c 0d 0e 0f
0010   10 11 12 13 14 15 16 17 18' ; done ) | text2pcap -u 42,42 -F blf - testrun/test-eth-3x-67b.blf

# The following ends up on too neat alignment when only existing on their own.
# To test, generate 3 can fd Frames ending up at odd offset, and then 4 and 5 frames
# of the evenly aligned fixed size object type to end up last in order.
# Count of 4 for structures with a size the multiple of 4, and count 5
# when the base object size increments by 2, e.g. flexray and ethernet

( for i in $(seq 1 3) ; do printf '0:00:00.%06d\n' $i ; echo '0000   00 00 00 e7 03 05 00 00 00 11 22' ; done ) | text2pcap -E socketcan - testrun/stage-canfd-3x-3b.pcapng
( for i in $(seq 1 4) ; do printf '0:00:00.%06d\n' $i ; echo '0000   00 00 00 e7 03 00 00 00 00 11 22' ; done ) | text2pcap -E socketcan - testrun/stage-can-4x-3b.pcapng
( for i in $(seq 1 4) ; do printf '0:00:00.%06d\n' $i ; echo '0000   01 00 00 00 30 12 00 00 00 11 22' ; done ) | text2pcap -E lin - testrun/stage-lin-4x-3b.pcapng
( for i in $(seq 1 4) ; do printf '0:00:00.%06d\n' $i ; echo '0000   01 00 00 e7 06 00 2a 00 11 22 33 44 55' ; done ) | text2pcap -E flexray - testrun/stage-flexray-4x-6b.pcapng
( for i in $(seq 1 5) ; do printf '0:00:00.%06d\n' $i ; echo '0000   01 00 00 e7 06 00 2a 00 11 22 33 44 55' ; done ) | text2pcap -E flexray - testrun/stage-flexray-5x-6b.pcapng
( for i in $(seq 1 4) ; do printf '0:00:00.%06d\n' $i ; echo '0000   00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09 0a 0b 0c 0d 0e 0f
0010   10 11 12 13 14 15 16 17 18' ; done ) | text2pcap -u 42,42 - testrun/stage-eth-4x-67b.pcapng
( for i in $(seq 1 5) ; do printf '0:00:00.%06d\n' $i ; echo '0000   00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09 0a 0b 0c 0d 0e 0f
0010   10 11 12 13 14 15 16 17 18' ; done ) | text2pcap -u 42,42 - testrun/stage-eth-5x-67b.pcapng

mergecap -F blf -w testrun/test-merged-canfd-can4x.blf testrun/stage-canfd-3x-3b.pcapng testrun/stage-can-4x-3b.pcapng
mergecap -F blf -w testrun/test-merged-canfd-lin4x.blf testrun/stage-canfd-3x-3b.pcapng testrun/stage-lin-4x-3b.pcapng
mergecap -F blf -w testrun/test-merged-canfd-flexray4x.blf testrun/stage-canfd-3x-3b.pcapng testrun/stage-flexray-4x-6b.pcapng
mergecap -F blf -w testrun/test-merged-canfd-flexray5x.blf testrun/stage-canfd-3x-3b.pcapng testrun/stage-flexray-5x-6b.pcapng
mergecap -F blf -w testrun/test-merged-canfd-eth4x.blf testrun/stage-canfd-3x-3b.pcapng testrun/stage-eth-4x-67b.pcapng
mergecap -F blf -w testrun/test-merged-canfd-eth5x.blf testrun/stage-canfd-3x-3b.pcapng testrun/stage-eth-5x-67b.pcapng
```

Prior to patch only the files containing only LIN data was succesfully opened, but as soon as they were combined with CAN FD the resulting files also failed to open.
The latest released version does not support CAN XL, but the generated files with the patch does work to open both in head of master and other tools.

Can the padding be added when writing the current container, rather than retroactively added once you need to write an additional container after a container? If so, should it, or are there problems with doing that?

The padding itself is written just as you are about to close the container, so the padding itself ends up in the actual order of writing (at end of file). The only backtracking needed is to go back to the last object of the container to claim the padding space in the last block header, as having a container with a size != the sum of its contained blocks creates other issues.

The blocks/objects themselves (most of them) are fine not being 4 byte aligned, it's mainly the log container that has issues.

Oh, and closing the log container does happen more times than at the end of the file, once a log container has filled to the size defined (10MB) the container is closed and a new one is opened for the following objects to come.
